title: Speed up local overlap inventory parsing without changing coverage
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

`find_overlap.py` scans a large Git tree to report missing local research notes. Its HEAD-inventory loop previously constructed a `PurePosixPath` for every entry, including nested vendor and evidence files outside the inventory. Filter canonical Git path strings first and parse metadata only for matching paths. Retain the same HEAD binding, regular modes, searched-note set, omission reporting and warnings, with no cache.

This is tooling. Local measurements on the same 129,156-entry tree and 8,917-note corpus gave median HEAD-inventory time 0.512789s -> 0.178231s and complete local scan 1.673241s -> 1.350239s across seven alternating trials. Complete records, coverage and warnings matched in every trial. Timings are local observations on Linux WSL2 / CPython 3.10.12, not scientific replay or network-refresh gains. No new kappa or supplier admission; the selected frontier and its five framework assumptions are unchanged.

## Task and overlap

Base: `7c49fe32c55de02c2c873655c804b16e4c3fef0a`, priority revision 8. Task `replay-runtime`, scope key `b1dd41940c60d240b47a`, chooser nonce `2f902f02bc90b13cafed87d51f51b71d`. Scope is **changed** from scientific replay profiling to coordination-tool runtime, reducing measured overhead in the required research-overlap procedure.

Read start-here #1163, live handoffs #1166 and active discussions/open PRs before selection. The paginated overlap snapshot covered 760 open PR bodies and 6,881 discussion records, fetched 2026-11-06 at 20:03:19 UTC and 20:05:44 UTC. Live handoffs/discussion listings and targeted open-PR searches were rechecked before publication; canonical main remains the base above. No competing inventory-parsing optimization found within that coverage. This is not a novelty certificate; code diffs and unpublished work are outside the search.

The existing local-coverage contract in `docs/research/coordination.md` remains the authority. Earlier overlap-search optimizations address different stages; this change only removes avoidable path-object and metadata parsing from `local_coverage`.

## Validation

- `python3 -B scripts/research_selected_baseline.py`: `PASS_RESEARCH_BASELINE_BINDINGS_ONLY`.
- `python3 -B -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_research_overlap*.py'`: 38 passed.
- Same suite under `python3 -O -B`: 38 passed.
- All 17 `test_research_*.py` modules containing `find_overlap`, serially through `run_isolated_tests.run_modules`, workers=1, module_timeout=60: passed. Includes Git-root binding, aliases, cache/pagination and Unicode excerpts.
- `git diff --check`: passed.

The new genuine-Git fixture retains Unicode/space/tab/newline names, executable and ordinary blobs, excludes a committed symlink and nested vendor/arbitrary files, then checks that deleting the executable note exposes its exact missing path. Existing sparse-checkout and failure controls remain in place. Some broader fixture tests inherited interactive GPG signing; initial runs were stopped, and the completed run used a temporary PATH wrapper executing `/usr/bin/git -c commit.gpgsign=false "$@"`. User configuration was unchanged.

`docs/research/overlap-inventory-runtime.md` includes the reproducible before/after benchmark and remaining scope. No native/operator, Lean, Docker or historical scientific suite was run for this coordination-only edit. No hosted CI or independent human review is claimed.

## Credit

Credit Douglas Colkitt and retained overlap-helper/coverage contributors. Apache-2.0; substantial OpenAI Codex assistance in implementation, verification and writing. Tests and local timings are author-generated evidence.

## Open next questions

Reading and validating working-tree notes is the larger remaining local cost. Measure that stage before proposing another optimization; preserve alias rejection, working edits and untracked notes. A HEAD-only cache would lose those obligations. No follow-on task is reserved.
